hints: Think about changing the conditions around the enemy.
A grower might arrange for help when the weather will not provide it.
Nine letters: describes land after water has been supplied to it.
bingo-arid-1.explanation: Supplying land with water directly counters its lack of rainfall or moisture.

hints: Imagine finding something neglected that is still worth saving.
A skilled craftsperson could bring it back towards its former condition.
Eleven letters: the name for that process of bringing something back.
bingo-rot-1.explanation: Bringing something back into good condition counters its decay.

hints: Think about what could get a stalled effort going again.
It needs a fresh supply of energy or enthusiasm.
Twelve letters, a verb beginning RE: give something renewed vitality.
bingo-inert-1.explanation: Giving renewed energy or vitality counters being slow and apathetic.

hints: Think about a different approach to sharing what you have.
Picture giving freely, without holding anything back.
Twelve letters, ending LY: describes giving without limiting the amount.
bingo-stingy-1.explanation: Giving freely, without restricting the amount, is the opposite of being unwilling to give.

hints: Think about the quality a careful investigator wants in an account.
What matters is whether it is grounded in what actually happened.
Eleven letters, ending NESS: the quality of being based on facts.
bingo-false-1.explanation: Being actual and based on fact is the opposite of being false.

hints: Picture the mood after a tense gathering starts to enjoy itself.
Think of a comparison: the mood has become more cheerful.
Seven letters: more festive or full of good cheer.
bingo-ire-1.explanation: A more cheerful, good-humoured mood counters anger.

hints: Sometimes the right words can take away an unsettling feeling.
Someone worried about what might happen could need this from a trusted friend.
Eleven letters: something said or done to restore confidence and ease fear.
bingo-scare-1.explanation: Restoring confidence and easing fear counters a fright.

hints: Think about the person who sees how all the pieces should fit together.
Behind a smoothly run operation, someone has planned and directed it.
Eleven letters: plans and directs something skilfully, as a verb.
bingo-mess-1.explanation: Planning and directing an operation brings organisation to disorder.

hints: Try a different way of looking at the person on the receiving end.
Imagine understanding their feelings as though you were in their position.
Ten letters, British spelling: understands and shares another person’s feelings.
bingo-spite-1.explanation: Understanding another person’s feelings counters the wish to hurt them.

hints: Think about changing the conditions that let something become unsafe.
Clean water and the removal of waste can be part of it.
Ten letters: making conditions clean and hygienic to protect health.
bingo-taint-1.explanation: Making things clean and free of harmful germs counters contamination.
